ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity white pixels occupy approximately 70% of the visible surface area against 30% low-intensity black pixels located primarily at the periphery and central fluke base.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant contiguous white fields across both lobes. A central low-intensity black vertical band originates from the notch area. High-intensity black bordering is observed along the trailing edges. Discrete black spotting/mottling is localized in the lower-central quadrant of the right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Central V-shaped depression; upper angle clearly visible at approximately 45 degrees, though the vertex is partially occluded by water spray.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations along the trailing edge of both lobes; amplitude of peaks varies between 3-12 pixels relative to the mean edge line; more prominent on the distal half of the right lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Bilateral convex curvature; the right lobe exhibits a sharp upward sweep ending in an acute distal tip; the left lobe displays a similar convex sweep but is partially truncated by the water line.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Clusters of high-contrast, roughly circular white/tan pixel groups (barnacles) are detected at the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several fine, dark-pigmented linear marks (rake marks) are visible on the mid-section of the right lobe, oriented diagonally to the fluke's main axis.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Localized barnacle colonization at the fluke tips and distinct parallel linear scarring (rake marks) on the ventral surface of the right lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Presence of multiple foreground avian subjects (cormorants) and localized water turbulence masking the central insertion point of the fluke.
